sections.html:
Davenport, the Scott County seat, stands on the Mississippi at Iowa's eastern edge. It belongs to the Quad Cities, a group of five that also takes in Bettendorf in Iowa and Rock Island, Moline and East Moline in Illinois. The metro area holds 381,801 people.

The city spreads over about 66 square miles at 660 feet. The river runs east to west here and the ground climbs toward the north. The 2020 count was 101,724 residents, third in Iowa behind Des Moines and Cedar Rapids. Population has hovered near 100,000 for roughly four decades, so a seller should not count on a rush of new arrivals. Condition and price carry the sale.

Three bridges link Davenport to Illinois, the Government Bridge, the Centennial Bridge and the I-280 Bridge, and many buyers commute across them. The nearest commercial airport is Quad City International in Moline.

Davenport has no permanent flood wall or levee, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi River without one. An older flood wall dates from 1919. The city requires new construction in the floodplain to be raised or protected by walls.

YearWhat happened
1993The Great Flood crested at 22.63 feet on July 9, nearly 8 feet above flood stage
2008Credit Island stayed closed for 5.5 months after the flooding
2019The river flooded again, while higher walls protected downtown Rock Island and Bettendorf
2023The river flooded again

Anyone selling a riverside house should expect buyers to ask whether the lot is in a floodplain and whether the house has ever taken water. A cash buyer asks the same questions but can price the answer in directly, without waiting on an insurer or a lender's review.

Davenport has several historic districts, and a house inside one may carry expectations about its look and age. Three stand out.

  • Hamburg Historic District: home to the most architecturally significant residences in the old German neighborhoods.
  • Vander Veer Park Historic District: anchored by Vander Veer Park, which was modeled on New York's Central Park.
  • Village of East Davenport: its Lindsay Park served as a Civil War parade ground for Camp McClellan.

The east side has long held higher-end housing. Whatever the area, a seller of an older house should collect permits, repair receipts and any flood history before talking with buyers.

The Davenport Community School District serves nearly 14,500 students across Davenport, Blue Grass, Buffalo and Walcott, which makes it the fourth largest district in Iowa. It runs four public high schools (Central, West, Mid City and North), six intermediate schools and 23 elementary schools. Assumption is the private high school.

St. Ambrose University, Palmer College of Chiropractic, Kaplan University and Hamilton Technical College are also in town. A house near a campus or school may attract a different set of buyers than one near the river, so describe its location plainly.

The main Iowa charge at recording is the real estate transfer tax. Iowa Code 428A.1 puts it at 80 cents per $500 of value, and a transfer made without consideration is exempt.

Property tax is a separate bill. The dates come from Iowa Code 445.37: installment one lapses October 1 and installment two April 1. A payment made online has to be entered before midnight ending the prior month, and when a weekend gets in the way the deadline shifts.

  • Ask the Scott County Treasurer which installments are paid.
  • Have the title company prorate the current bill to the closing date.
  • Confirm the groundwater hazard statement is signed before the deed goes to the recorder.

sections.h2: What to gather before talking to buyers
sections.html:
A short folder of records answers most buyer questions about a Davenport house.

  • Any flood insurance policy, claim or repair receipt, since the Mississippi flooded in 1993, 2008, 2019 and 2023.
  • Elevation or floodplain information for the lot, because new floodplain construction has to be raised or walled.
  • Records on wells, tanks or a septic system, for the groundwater hazard statement.
  • Lease copies and rent status if tenants live in the house.

If a house needs more repair than you want to fund, say so at the start. A cash buyer prices the work, while a conventional buyer's inspection usually turns it into a negotiation.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Davenport house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the listing, the open houses and the lender's timeline. Start by describing the address and the shape the house is in. A written offer follows, and the closing date is one you choose.

Next a title company or attorney drafts the deed and filings. The buyer pays at closing, and the deed is recorded in Scott County. Declining costs nothing, so measure the offer against what a listing would leave you after repairs and agent fees.

If the house has tenants, an inherited title or a payoff owed on it, mention that on the first call. Each of these changes the paperwork, though the steps stay the same, and the title company sorts out liens and balances from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Repair it or sell it as it stands?
sections.html:
Many Davenport houses are old, and many sit within reach of a river that has flooded in 1993, 2008, 2019 and 2023. That combination makes the repair question real. A basement that has taken water, a worn roof or a furnace near the end of its life can each cost a seller months of effort before a conventional listing even begins.

Start by listing what is wrong with the house, from the biggest item down. Then think about who will pay for each fix. In a traditional sale the buyer's inspector writes the list and you negotiate credits or do the work. In a cash sale the buyer looks at the same list but folds it into the price at the start, so there is one negotiation and one number to accept or decline.

Neither route is right for every owner. If the house needs little and you are in no hurry, listing may bring more. If you are short on time, money or patience for repairs, a cash offer trades some price for certainty.

sections.h2: Timeline from first call to recording
sections.html:
The order of events is the same for most sellers. First you describe the house and get a written offer. If you accept, a closing date is set with a title company or attorney, who searches title and checks for liens. Before the date, you collect the papers listed above, contact the Scott County Treasurer about the tax bill and arrange final utility readings.

At closing you sign the deed and the declaration of value, and the groundwater hazard statement if the property has anything to report. The deed is then recorded in Scott County. The tax share and any loan balance come out of the proceeds, and you receive the rest.

faqs.q: How many people live in Davenport, Iowa?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 101,724, which made Davenport the third most populous city in Iowa. The metro area had 381,801 people.

faqs.q: Does Davenport have a flood wall?
faqs.a: No permanent flood wall or levee protects the city, which makes it the largest city on the Mississippi without one. New construction in the floodplain must be raised or walled.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Davenport home sale?
faqs.a: Under Iowa Code 428A.1 the rate is 80 cents per $500 of value. A transfer with no consideration owes nothing.
The Davenport Community School District serves nearly 14,500 students across Davenport, Blue Grass, Buffalo and Walcott. It is the fourth largest district in Iowa.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: Installment one lapses on October 1 and installment two on April 1. If a weekend interferes, the date becomes the second business day of that month.
